title: The adjoint section of the normalized universal module
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field, let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over $k$ with a $k$-rational point $\sigma$, let $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{X/k}$, and let $D_{\mathrm{univ}}\subset H\times_kX$ be the universal effective Cartier divisor [lem-pc-universal-divisor]. Put $\mathcal L_H:=\mathcal O(D_{\mathrm{univ}})\otimes\operatorname{pr}_H^*\sigma_H^*\mathcal O(D_{\mathrm{univ}})^{-1}$. Let $W\subseteq H$ be the maximal open on which $\mathcal L_H|_{W\times_kX}$ belongs to the Picard open subfunctor $F(W)$ [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor], and write $f_W:W\times_kX\to W$ and $\mathcal N_W:=f_{W,*}(\mathcal L_H|_{W\times_kX})$. Then $\mathcal N_W$ is invertible and the section corresponding under tensor--Hom adjunction to the counit $f_W^*\mathcal N_W\to\mathcal L_H|_{W\times_kX}$ has zero scheme $D_{\mathrm{univ}}|_{W\times_kX}$.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor] the inclusion $F\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable by open immersions; applied to $\mathcal L_H\in\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(H)$ this gives the maximal open $W\subseteq H$ with $\mathcal L_W:=\mathcal L_H|_{W\times X}\in F(W)$. By the definition of $F$ there is an invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module $\mathcal N$ with $Rf_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N[0]$; taking $H^0$, $\mathcal N_W=f_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N$ is invertible and $Rf_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N_W[0]$. Let $\varphi:f_W^*\mathcal N_W\to\mathcal L_W$ be the counit and $s_{\mathrm{adj}}$ the corresponding section of $\mathcal L_W\otimes f_W^*\mathcal N_W^{-1}$; its zero scheme is $Z(\varphi)$ [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso]. The hypotheses of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-recd] ($T=W$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_W\in F(W)$, $\mathcal N=\mathcal N_W$ invertible with $Rf_{W,*}\mathcal L_W\cong\mathcal N_W[0]$) hold, so $Z(\varphi)$ is a closed subscheme of $W\times X$ finite locally free of degree $g$ over $W$, i.e. a point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$.

proof.text: Write $D_W:=D_{\mathrm{univ}}|_{W\times X}$ and $\mathcal M:=\sigma_W^*\mathcal O(D_W)^{-1}$, so $\mathcal L_W=\mathcal O(D_W)\otimes f_W^*\mathcal M$ by definition. By [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme] the canonical section $1_D$ of $\mathcal O(D_W)$ has $Z(1_D)=D_W$; hence $s_1:=1_D\otimes\mathrm{id}:f_W^*\mathcal M\to\mathcal L_W$ has $Z(s_1)=D_W$ (locally $s_1$ is multiplication by the same local equation, $f_W^*\mathcal M$ being invertible). By adjunction $s_1=\varphi\circ f_W^*t$ for $t:\mathcal M\to f_{W,*}\mathcal L_W$ adjoint to $s_1$; locally $s_1$ is multiplication by $b\,c$ where $\varphi$ is multiplication by $b$, so $\mathcal I_{Z(s_1)}\subseteq\mathcal I_{Z(\varphi)}$, i.e. $Z(\varphi)\subseteq D_W$. Since $D_{\mathrm{univ}}$ is the universal point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}$ [lem-pc-universal-divisor], $D_W$ is also a point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$, and two nested points of $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{X/k}(W)$ are equal [lem-pc-hilb-nested-points-equal]. Hence $Z(s_{\mathrm{adj}})=Z(\varphi)=D_W$.
